episodes.title: First Meeting Today
episodes.text: You sit down with two applicants for their first meeting. You start gathering details for their loan application.

choice.prompt: They did not bring proof of income. Do you keep going or pause?

options.label: Keep gathering what you can
options.outcome: You take down their job details and housing costs. You make a note to collect the pay papers later.

options.label: Pause and wait for papers
options.outcome: You stop the form where it is. You set a time for them to come back with the missing papers.

chat.text: We filled out what we could. What else do you need from us?
And how long does this application part usually take?

episodes.title: Talking Through Options
episodes.text: You sit with an applicant who is confused by the choices. You walk through the different loan types and credit options. You explain the terms in plain words and answer questions.

trial.title: Check if a loan fits
items: Decide if the loan looks feasible
trial.explain: You look at money and credit first, then the property, before you decide.

episodes.title: Sending Same Forms
episodes.text: You send finished applications to the credit analyst. You attach the same information sheet you sent yesterday. You wait for the confirmation back. Tomorrow you will do it again.

episodes.title: Reading The Numbers
episodes.text: You sit quietly with a file open. You compare income and debts against the credit report. You read the property evaluation and note whether the loan looks feasible.

episodes.title: Over Your Limit
episodes.text: You review a request that is over the amount you can approve. You know it has to go to management.

choice.prompt: The applicant wants an answer now. What do you do?

options.label: Explain and refer to management
options.outcome: You tell them you cannot approve this size yourself. You send the file to management for a decision.

options.label: Approve it yourself anyway
options.outcome: You sign past your limit. The approval is invalid and management has to undo it.

chat.text: That amount is past what we can sign off, right?
Yes. Send me the file and I will take it from here.

episodes.title: Files To Verification
episodes.text: You gather the last applications of the day. You submit them to the credit analyst for verification and recommendation. You log that they are sent and waiting.

episodes.title: Opening Today's Animation
episodes.text: You arrive and open your computer to start today's graphics and animation. You review the brief and use your own judgment to shape the look. You begin building the complex pieces frame by frame.

episodes.title: Saving Version Files
episodes.text: You sit down to update the configuration control system. You name the files, log the versions, and file them in the same folders as yesterday. Same again tomorrow.

episodes.title: Checking Campaign Progress
episodes.text: You join a quick check-in on the multimedia campaign to track progress.

choice.prompt: The tracker is behind and backgrounds are late. What do you update first?

options.label: Update the tracker now
options.outcome: You log what is done and what is late. Everyone sees the same list for the afternoon.

options.label: Finish a background first
options.outcome: You finish one background design, then update the tracker late. The list is accurate but posted later.

chat.text: Where are we on background design?
Can you update the progress tracker before lunch?
I can help with production coordination if you list what's left.

episodes.title: Drawing Carton Illustrations
episodes.text: You sit down to create basic drawings for a product carton. You sketch the illustration by hand, then refine it on the computer. You size it to fit the label space.

trial.title: Spot the label problem
trial.scenario: You check your illustration against the carton brief. The drawing is clean, but the product name touches the fold edge and will get cut off.
options: Move the product name away from the fold
Add more color to the illustration
Make the drawing lines thinner
trial.explain: The name must stay clear of the fold to print correctly.

episodes.title: Tight Deadline Sequence
episodes.text: You script and plan a short animated sequence that is due today. You draw key poses by hand, then build them in software. The clock keeps moving while you work.

choice.prompt: You are running out of time on the sequence. What do you do?

options.label: Lock the script and animate
options.outcome: You stop changing the plan and finish the shots. The sequence is simple but complete on time.

options.label: Keep reworking the plan
options.outcome: You spend more time on the script and have less time to animate. You rush the final shots to deliver.

options.label: Cut one shot and tell production
options.outcome: You remove one shot and note it for coordination. The shorter sequence renders and delivers on time.

episodes.title: Budget and Schedule Notes
episodes.text: You open the campaign budget and schedule sheet. You log today's hours and check what is left for production. You save the file and close out the day.

episodes.title: Morning Truck Check
episodes.text: You walk around the truck in the lot. You check gas, oil, water, tires, lights, and brakes. You top off the washer fluid and note the tread looks fine.

trial.title: Spot what needs attention
trial.scenario: You finish the walk-around. The left tires look full, lights and brakes test fine, but the right rear tire is visibly low.
options: Right rear tire is low
Oil level is fine
Headlights turn on
trial.explain: The low tire is the one thing that needs attention before driving.

episodes.title: Checking the Load
episodes.text: You open the back doors and pull out the shipping papers. You count boxes and match each line on the list. Everything on the paper is on the truck.

episodes.title: Following the Route
episodes.text: You sit in the cab and read the map for the first stop. You follow the written directions street by street. You watch for the turn after the bridge.

choice.prompt: The written directions say right after the bridge, but the road sign looks different. What do you do?

options.label: Take the marked right as written
options.outcome: You turn right and stay on the planned route. You keep driving toward the address.

options.label: Stop and re-read the map
options.outcome: You pull over and re-read the directions. You confirm the turn before moving again.

episodes.title: Midday Highway Miles
episodes.text: You stay in lane and keep your speed steady. You stop at the lights and signal every turn. Same as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Strange Engine Noise
episodes.text: You hear a rattle up front and pull into a lot. You see the temperature gauge is climbing.

choice.prompt: You need to decide what to do about the possible mechanical problem.

options.label: Report it now and stay parked
options.outcome: You call in the problem and stay parked. Help brings supplies and checks the truck.

options.label: Keep driving to the next stop
options.outcome: You drive on slowly while watching the gauge. You report the noise when you arrive.

chat.text: What are you hearing?
Can you still drive it safe?
Want me to bring water and oil?

episodes.title: Customer Gives Directions
episodes.text: You roll down the window at the new building. The customer gives you verbal directions to the back entrance. You follow them around the block and park where they point.

episodes.title: Morning Orders Check
episodes.text: You arrive and sit down at the desk. You open the day's list of physician orders. You read each one to confirm the prescribed exam before anyone is called back.

episodes.title: Screening Questions
episodes.text: You call in your first patient and sit down with the screening form.

chat.text: Do I need to list my tattoo and implant?
Yes, please tell me about anything metal, implants, or pregnancy.
I have a tattoo on my shoulder and a knee replacement.

episodes.title: Choosing Coil Setup
episodes.text: You look back at the confirmed order for the next exam. You select the imaging technique and coil that will produce the required images. You set them up by the scanner.

choice.prompt: The order is not clear about which area to image. What do you do?

options.label: Pause and check the order again
options.outcome: You re-read the order and call to clarify. The exam starts a little late but matches the prescription.

options.label: Guess and set up anyway
options.outcome: You set up for the wrong area. You have to stop, redo the setup, and recheck the order.

episodes.title: Running Afternoon Scans
episodes.text: You operate the MRI scanner through the afternoon list. You run one exam, then the next in the same way. It is the same as yesterday and will be the same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Pacemaker Flag
episodes.text: You are screening a patient when he mentions a cardiac pacemaker. You stop the intake interview. You do not send him toward the scanner room.

choice.prompt: The patient has a cardiac pacemaker and is scheduled for an MRI. What do you do?

options.label: Hold the exam and flag the order
options.outcome: You keep the patient out of the scanner area. You note the pacemaker and send the order back for review.

options.label: Ask about other metal and pregnancy too
options.outcome: You finish asking about ferrous objects, prosthetic valves, and pregnancy. You still hold the exam because of the pacemaker.

options.label: Let him wait by the scanner
options.outcome: He waits near the magnet with a pacemaker in place. You move him back out and hold the exam.

episodes.title: Easing The Noise
episodes.text: You help your last patient onto the table. You see her tense at the loud knocking sound. You offer comfort for the noise during the scan.

trial.title: Reply about the noise
trial.says: That banging is really unpleasant. Is there anything for my ears?
options: I can give you headphones or earplugs to reduce the noise.
Just try to ignore the noise and lie still.
We can skip the scan if the noise bothers you.
trial.explain: Offering headphones or earplugs is the professional way to reduce unpleasant noise.

episodes.title: Checking New Arrival
episodes.text: You arrive at the back room and put on gloves. You sit down with the new box at the examination table. You study the object closely to check its origin and history.

episodes.title: Answering Public Question
episodes.text: You sit down at the front desk computer. A visitor needs information from the holdings.

choice.prompt: The visitor wants details from the holdings. How do you answer?

options.label: Look up the holdings and explain what you find
options.outcome: You pull up the records and walk through what the museum holds. The visitor leaves with clear information.

options.label: Answer quickly from memory without checking
options.outcome: You give a short answer and the visitor leaves unsure. You make a note to check the records later.

chat.text: Do you have anything on the old river mill tools?
I want to know what you hold and where it came from.

episodes.title: Laying Out Exhibit
episodes.text: You walk into the small gallery with the theme notes. You sort the exhibit materials on the table. You test how the pieces will sit together before you install them.

trial.title: Put exhibit in order
items: Install the exhibit materials in the space
Select the exhibition theme and design
Plan the storage and layout of the pieces
trial.explain: You pick the theme first, then plan, make, and install.

episodes.title: Cataloging Records Again
episodes.text: You sit back down at the database. You enter the same registration fields you entered yesterday. You save each record and move to the next line. Same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Storage Problem Found
episodes.text: You open the storage cabinet and see water under a boxed collection. You lift the box and check what got damp. You need to decide how to protect the rest.

choice.prompt: The storage area is wet and more boxes are at risk. What do you do first?

options.label: Move the dry boxes to safe storage now
options.outcome: You carry the dry boxes to another shelf and log the move. The wet box stays aside for drying.

options.label: Leave everything and finish the exhibit work
options.outcome: You go back to the gallery and the damp spreads. You return later to a bigger mess.

options.label: Ask a colleague to help move and check
options.outcome: You both move the boxes and check each one. The work goes faster with two pairs of hands.

episodes.title: Quiet Research Hour
episodes.text: You return to your desk and open your research notes. You read through your area of interest and compare sources. You write down what you still need to check.

episodes.title: Morning Group Lesson
episodes.text: You arrive and set out chairs for the small morning group. You demonstrate a short rhythm and ask them to play it back. You lead a quick discussion about what felt steady and what did not.

episodes.title: Changing the Plan
episodes.text: You sit down with one student who is not following the worksheet. You see she watches your hands more than the page. You pause and consider how to change the material for her.

choice.prompt: She keeps losing her place on the page. What do you do now?

options.label: Show it first, then read it
options.outcome: You play the line slowly while she watches, then you point to each note together. She plays two bars through without stopping.

options.label: Stay with the worksheet
options.outcome: You keep pointing to the page and she keeps stopping halfway. You both spend the rest of the time on the same four measures.

episodes.title: Watching and Listening
episodes.text: You sit to the side while two students play in turn. You watch their hands and listen for timing and tone. You note each student's ease, limits, and interest as they play.

trial.title: Who needs help first
trial.scenario: You observe two students. One plays steadily but looks bored. The other rushes, misses notes, and grips tightly.
options: The student who rushes and grips tightly
The student who plays steadily
Both are fine for now
trial.explain: The tense grip and missed notes show a limit that needs attention first.

episodes.title: Same Daily Records
episodes.text: You sit down with the attendance and lesson log. You enter who came and what you covered, same boxes as yesterday. You check the names twice and close the binder.

episodes.title: Hard Part Frustration
episodes.text: You work with a student stuck on a difficult passage. He puts his instrument down and says he cannot get it. You feel the lesson stalling as he pulls back.

choice.prompt: He says he wants to skip the hard part for good. What do you say?

options.label: Break it small and try again
options.outcome: You set two measures at a slow pace and he plays them three times. He still struggles, but he picks the instrument back up.

options.label: Let him drop the piece
options.outcome: You move on to an easier song and the tension drops. The hard passage stays unplayed in his folder.

episodes.title: Talking About Next
episodes.text: You meet with an older student after her lesson. You talk about what she could try next to keep learning. You encourage her to keep at the challenging piece a little longer.

episodes.title: Wiping Down Tables
episodes.text: You arrive and wipe down the table and chairs with cleaner. You soak the metal tools and lay out fresh files. It is the same wipe and soak as yesterday, and the same again tomorrow.

episodes.title: Shaping Morning Nails
episodes.text: You sit down with your first client of the day. You trim the ends with scissors and file them even. You smooth each edge with an emery board until nothing catches.

episodes.title: Softening Tough Cuticles
episodes.text: You soak her fingertips in warm water and dab on oil. You pick up the cuticle knife to start pushing back.

choice.prompt: Her cuticle edge looks red and sore. Do you trim it now?

options.label: Just push it back gently and skip trimming
options.outcome: You push the skin back with the knife and leave the sore spot alone. You move on without any bleeding.

options.label: Trim the sore edge with nippers
options.outcome: You nip the sore edge and it starts to bleed a little. You press it clean and stop trimming that finger.

chat.text: My cuticles always feel dry and tight.
Is it okay to just cut them all off?

episodes.title: Painting Nails Blue
episodes.text: You sit down to polish after the nails are shaped. You brush on a thin undercoat and let it set. You brush on the blue color and finish with a clear coat.

trial.title: Order the polish job
items: Brush on the clear top layer
trial.explain: Undercoat goes first, then color, then clear.

episodes.title: Smudged Fresh Polish
episodes.text: You look down and see a thumb polish is smudged and streaked. The brush left a thick line and the wet layer dragged. The client is waiting while the polish is still wet.

choice.prompt: The wet polish is smudged. What do you do?

options.label: Smooth more polish over the smudge
options.outcome: You brush more polish over the wet smudge. The streak stays underneath and the layer looks thick.

options.label: Wipe it off and redo that nail
options.outcome: You wipe that nail clean and brush the undercoat and color on again. The nail matches the others after a few minutes.

options.label: Ask her to wait while it dries
options.outcome: You leave the smudged nail to dry as it is. It hardens with the streak still showing.

episodes.title: Counting Bottles Late
episodes.text: You sit at the back table with your notebook. You count polish bottles and clean files and write down what is low. You note each client service from today in the record book.

episodes.title: Checking the Playroom
episodes.text: You arrive at the nursery school and set your bag down. You walk the playroom and pick up stray blocks from yesterday. You straighten mats and corners so the space is safe to start.

episodes.title: Watching Morning Play
episodes.text: You sit on the low chair by the blocks. You watch the children build and push cars back and forth. You keep watching from the same spot, same as yesterday.

episodes.title: Helping Two Share
episodes.text: Two children both want the red truck and their voices rise. You kneel down beside them at their level. You help them name feelings and practice taking turns.

choice.prompt: Both children are upset over the truck. What do you do first?

options.label: Help them use words and take turns
options.outcome: They each say what they want and agree on turns. The play continues with less crying.

options.label: Take the truck away for now
options.outcome: They quiet down but both look sad. You sit with them until they are ready to try again.

episodes.title: Lunchtime in Group
episodes.text: You sit with the small group at the low tables in the nursery school. You stay close while they eat and wipe hands. You keep the routine calm and steady.

trial.title: What Needs Attention First
trial.scenario: You are monitoring play in the nursery room. Two children stack soft blocks quietly nearby. A third child climbs onto a wobbly shelf to reach a toy.
options: The child climbing on the wobbly shelf
The children stacking soft blocks quietly
The tidy book corner across the room
trial.explain: The climbing child can fall, so you keep the play space safe first.

episodes.title: Loose Mat Corner
episodes.text: You see the large play mat has folded up near the doorway. A toddler runs toward it while older kids chase past. You step in fast before anyone trips.

choice.prompt: The folded mat is in the running path. What do you do?

options.label: Stop the play and flatten the mat
options.outcome: The children pause while you smooth the mat flat. You invite them back once the floor is safe.

options.label: Guide children around it for now
options.outcome: You stand by the mat and steer feet around it. You fix the mat as soon as the rush passes.

episodes.title: Talking With Parents
episodes.text: You stand by the door as parents arrive for pickup. You share what you saw today.

chat.text: How was she today at play?
Did the sharing get any easier?

episodes.title: Morning Console Check
episodes.text: You arrive and sit down at the master console. You watch computer system and network performance on the screens. Everything looks steady for now.

trial.title: Spot the problem first
trial.scenario: You watch the master console for system and network performance. One server shows high lag, one workstation shows normal use. The network access line shows a failed login queue.
options: The server with high lag dragging performance down
The workstation showing normal use
A printer with paper loaded and ready
trial.explain: You check the lagging server first because it affects performance.

episodes.title: Email Access Help
episodes.text: You sit down with a coworker who cannot open email. You look at their email setup together.

choice.prompt: Their email settings look off and others can open email. Do you fix it now or keep checking?

options.label: Reconfigure their email now
options.outcome: You reset their email configuration and they reopen it. It loads and they send the files.

options.label: Check the whole email system first
options.outcome: You check the monitor and see the system is fine. You come back and fix their setup.

chat.text: My email just spins and never opens.
I need it to send my morning files.

episodes.title: Watching Virus Scans
episodes.text: You sit and watch the virus protection status screens. You check the same lists you checked yesterday. Nothing has changed and you keep watching.

episodes.title: Keeping Systems Updated
episodes.text: You walk through the computer room and check hardware and software. You update configurations and keep applications running. You note each change in place.

episodes.title: Network Connection Lost
episodes.text: You see a section of the network go offline. You test hardware and software to find the fault. A switch component has failed and needs replacing.

choice.prompt: You found the failed part. Do you replace it now or keep testing?

options.label: Replace the defective part now
options.outcome: You swap in the replacement part and the connection returns. Users log back on and work resumes.

options.label: Run one more diagnostic first
options.outcome: You run another test that confirms the same failed part. You then replace it and access returns.

options.label: Ask users to wait and reboot
options.outcome: You ask users to wait while you reboot the line. The fault stays until you replace the part.

episodes.title: Running Daily Backups
episodes.text: You sit back at the console and start data backups. You watch the copies complete and store. You keep the system ready for recovery if needed.

episodes.title: Picking Today's Tools
episodes.text: You sit down with coffee and open your laptop. You look at the small business site you need to update. You compare two authoring tools and scripting options for what fits best.

episodes.title: Building Homepage Layout
episodes.text: You open the content creation tool and drag the new photos into place. You adjust the homepage layout and save your changes. You preview it once to see it holds together.

episodes.title: Backing Up Files
episodes.text: You copy today's website files to your local folder. You wait for the progress bar to finish and check the date. Same as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Checking Code Everywhere
episodes.text: You sit down to evaluate the code you edited this morning. You run it through the checker and open it on different browsers. You note the menu looks wrong on phones and needs fixing.

trial.title: Spot the Break
trial.scenario: You preview the updated page on your laptop and tablet. It looks fine there, but on a phone the menu overlaps the text. The structure looks valid otherwise.
options: Menu code fails on small screens
Page title needs darker color
Backup folder needs new name
trial.explain: The menu overlap on phones shows a problem with device compatibility.

episodes.title: Adding Supporting Code
episodes.text: You open the site script to add the small contact form check. You see the code needs a few lines to handle empty fields. You pause on how to write it cleanly.

choice.prompt: How do you add the check for empty fields?

options.label: Write a short check now
options.outcome: You type the short check and test the form. Empty fields now show a simple message.

options.label: Reuse a longer snippet
options.outcome: You paste in the longer snippet and trim it down. The form works but takes extra testing.

episodes.title: Restoring Yesterday's Copy
episodes.text: The live site shows a blank page after an update. You open your local backup folder from this morning.

choice.prompt: The site is blank and you have a morning backup. What do you do?

options.label: Restore the backup now
options.outcome: You copy the backup files back to the site. The pages come back and you check them.

options.label: Try to fix the live code first
options.outcome: You spend twenty minutes looking at the live code. The site stays blank while you work.

chat.text: Site is showing blank. Do you have a copy?
Can you put it back for now?

episodes.title: Checking Today's Doses
episodes.text: You arrive and sit down at the computer to open the physician's prescriptions. You calculate each dose and measure what was received. You record what will be used and what is disposed.

episodes.title: First Injection
episodes.text: You check the order from the physician and prepare the syringe at the bedside. You explain the stick and administer the radiopharmaceutical intravenously. You watch the patient for a moment after the injection.

choice.prompt: The vein is thin and the first stick does not sit well. Do you push the dose or stop?

options.label: Push the dose through anyway
options.outcome: The dose leaks outside the vein. The images will be poor and you have to document the problem.

options.label: Stop and ask the physician what to do
options.outcome: You wait for direction. The injection is rescheduled and the dose is remeasured.

episodes.title: Logging Scan Results
episodes.text: You sit at the same computer and open the same log as yesterday. You type in the results of the morning procedures. Tomorrow you will do this again.

episodes.title: Processing Heart Images
episodes.text: You pull up the morning cardiac function study on the computer. You work through the images and process the heart function. You save the processed study for the record.

trial.title: Check the Heart Study
trial.scenario: You open a cardiac function study on the computer. One image is a little noisy but readable, and the patient name on the file does not match your log. The dose record matches the physician prescription.
options: Fix the noisy image first
Fix the wrong name first
Remeasure the dose first
trial.explain: The results cannot be processed under the wrong patient name.

episodes.title: Under the Camera
episodes.text: You help the patient onto the table and move the camera into place overhead. You tell them you need still pictures to map the medicine in the body.

chat.text: Do I have to lie still the whole time?
Will this camera touch me?
How long will the pictures take?

episodes.title: Dose Does Not Match
episodes.text: You measure the afternoon dose on the computer and compare it to the physician's prescription. The amount does not match what was ordered. You hold the syringe and do not inject.

choice.prompt: The measured dose does not match the prescription. What do you do now?

options.label: Give it anyway and note the difference
options.outcome: The record shows the wrong dose was given. The physician has to decide if the images can be used.

options.label: Hold the dose and check with the physician
options.outcome: You remeasure and rerecord with the physician. A corrected dose is ordered before anyone is injected.

options.label: Adjust the dose yourself to match
options.outcome: You change the amount without an order. The record is wrong and you have to report it.

episodes.title: Morning Turnover Walk
episodes.text: You arrive and take turnover at the controls. You walk the panels with the night operator. You check that the reactor is steady and the logs match procedures for worker and environmental safety.

episodes.title: Watching The Boards
episodes.text: You sit at the desk and watch flux, temperature, and power flow. Nothing moves much. You log the same readings you logged yesterday and will log tomorrow.

episodes.title: Moving Control Rods
episodes.text: You get the order to trim power a little. You stand at the controls and ready your hand on the rod switch. You watch flux level and reactor period as you prepare to move.

choice.prompt: The flux meter is slow to settle. Do you keep moving the rods or wait?

options.label: Wait and recheck the meters
options.outcome: You hold the rods and let flux and temperature settle. You make a smaller move once the readings are steady.

options.label: Keep inching the rods out
options.outcome: You make another small withdrawal and watch period shorten. You have to insert back to steady it.

episodes.title: Tagging Out Pump
episodes.text: You prepare a clearance so maintenance can repair a coolant pump. You hang locks and tags on the breakers and valves. You verify the equipment is isolated before you release it.

trial.title: Clear a pump for repair
items: Hang the lock and tag on the controls
Identify the pump and its isolation points
trial.explain: You identify, lock and tag, verify isolation, then release for repair.

episodes.title: Alarm On Panel
episodes.text: An alarm lights up and coolant temperature starts to drift. You move to the panel with the other operator.

choice.prompt: The procedure lists two likely causes. What do you do first?

options.label: Follow the procedure step for valve lineup
options.outcome: You check the valve positions and find one misaligned. You line it up and temperature stops rising.

options.label: Reduce power first to stabilize
options.outcome: You insert rods a little and temperature levels off. You still have to find the valve fault.

options.label: Call for a full emergency response
options.outcome: You announce the emergency lineup and the team stations. The readings stay within limits while you diagnose.

chat.text: Temp is up on loop B. Pressure is holding.
Work the abnormal procedure. Tell me cause and action.
You want me to pull the trend?

episodes.title: Guiding The Crew
episodes.text: You stand with the crew and direct positions per the emergency procedures. You tell each operator what to monitor and when to report. You keep everyone on the same steps until the unit is stable.

episodes.title: Morning History Review
episodes.text: You arrive and open the first charts of the day. You read through histories, symptoms, and physical findings. You compare them with the diagnostic information to work toward a diagnosis.

episodes.title: Explaining Health Risks
episodes.text: You sit down with a patient to go over ways to lower risk and prevent illness.

choice.prompt: She wants clear health information but seems overwhelmed. How do you give it?

options.label: Go over one small risk factor at a time
options.outcome: You explain one change clearly and she asks a few questions. You note what you covered for next time.

options.label: Cover all the prevention points at once
options.outcome: You go through everything quickly and she nods quietly. You give her a written summary to take home.

chat.text: I know I should change some habits, but I am not sure where to start.
Can you tell me what matters most for me right now?

episodes.title: Updating Patient Records
episodes.text: You sit at your desk and update health care plans and prognoses. You check each box and save each note. Same as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Writing Morning Prescriptions
episodes.text: You look over your morning notes to prescribe for two patients. You check age and gender before you decide on dosage, route, and frequency. You write each order down carefully.

trial.title: Put prescribing steps in order
items: Decide how often to give it
trial.explain: You check age and gender first, then set dosage, route, and frequency.

episodes.title: Conflicting Test Results
episodes.text: A patient's new symptoms and physical findings do not match the earlier history. The diagnostic information points in two directions. You need to settle on a diagnosis now so care can move forward.

choice.prompt: The findings conflict and time is short. What do you do?

options.label: Pause and re-analyze history and findings again
options.outcome: You go back through the history and findings line by line. You choose the diagnosis that best fits the full picture.

options.label: Stay with the first working diagnosis
options.outcome: You keep the earlier diagnosis and plan to recheck after the next findings come in. You note why you held to it.

episodes.title: Shaping Treatment Plans
episodes.text: You sit with your notes at the end of the day. You weigh scientific rationale, standards of care, and practice guidelines. You shape each treatment plan to fit what you found.

episodes.title: First Intake Today
episodes.text: You arrive and open a new client file. You sit down and ask about meals, diet restrictions, and current health plans. You start shaping a dietary-care plan from what you hear.

episodes.title: Morning Group Session
episodes.text: You lead a small group on healthy eating habits.

choice.prompt: The group looks unsure and one person has gone quiet. What do you do now?

options.label: Invite the quiet person to share one meal concern
options.outcome: They mention skipping breakfast and you talk through a simple morning habit together.

options.label: Keep explaining the basic rules to the whole group
options.outcome: You finish the basics and hand out notes for them to review later.

chat.text: I get confused about what good nutrition even means.
Do I have to give up everything I like?

episodes.title: Logging Food Records
episodes.text: You sit with the monitoring logs. You check yesterday's entries against the plans. Same form as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Family Kitchen Talk
episodes.text: You sit with a patient and their family. You walk through food selection and preparation for their new diet modifications. You answer questions about cooking at home.

trial.title: Answering a family worry
trial.says: We cook the same meals for everyone at home. How do we make this diet work for us?
options: Just make separate meals and follow the plan exactly.
Let's look at your family meals and adjust selection and preparation together.
Stop worrying about cooking and just follow the handout.
trial.explain: Good counseling adjusts food selection and preparation with the family.

episodes.title: Lab Result Change
episodes.text: You open the afternoon lab tests before updating recommendations. One result does not match the current nutrition plan. You need to decide how to change the recommendation.

choice.prompt: The lab result means the current plan needs a change. What do you do?

options.label: Revise the nutrition recommendation now to fit the lab result
options.outcome: You update the plan and explain the change to the patient clearly.

options.label: Hold the plan and recheck with a repeat test first
options.outcome: You keep meals steady for now and note to review after the next result.

episodes.title: Cultural Plan Notes
episodes.text: You finish notes for a nutrition plan. You write in the cultural and religious food preferences you discussed. You file the recommendations for tomorrow.

episodes.title: Morning Evaluation
episodes.text: You arrive at the hospital therapy room. You sit down with a new patient and test his grip, balance, and memory. You look at his medical notes to set a realistic rehab goal.

episodes.title: Choosing Today's Activity
episodes.text: You review what the patient can safely do right now. You pick a dressing and cooking task that fits his limits. You set out the tools where he can reach them.

trial.title: Set a rehab goal
trial.explain: You look at the records and test abilities before you set the goal.

episodes.title: Work Skills Group
episodes.text: You lead a small group practicing school and work skills. One woman wants to try typing, but her hands tire quickly. You decide how to adjust the task for her.

choice.prompt: She wants to keep typing through the pain. What do you do?

options.label: Shorten the typing and add rest breaks
options.outcome: She finishes the session without pain and practices pacing for work.

options.label: Switch her to a short sorting task
options.outcome: She rests her hands and still practices focus and work habits.

episodes.title: Afternoon Exercise Round
episodes.text: You run the same guided movement group as yesterday. You walk patients through the set routine step by step. Same tomorrow.

episodes.title: When Progress Stalls
episodes.text: You are with a patient who shuts down during the life-skills practice.

choice.prompt: He wants to stop the session early. What do you do?

options.label: Pause and simplify the task with him
options.outcome: He tries the smaller step and stays for the rest of the session.

options.label: Stop and sit with him to reset
options.outcome: He calms down and you plan a gentler task for next time.

options.label: Encourage one more short try together
options.outcome: He attempts once more, then you end on what he managed.

chat.text: I can't do this. This isn't working.
I just want to quit for today.

episodes.title: Updating Patient Records
episodes.text: You sit down at the desk to finish your notes. You write up today's tests, goals, and progress. You file each record before you leave.

episodes.title: The core work
episodes.text: You start the main work of a Online Course Creator — the core of the job, done properly, start to finish. No audience and no shortcut: this is the thing everything else in the day supports. This is the work the whole job is built around.

episodes.title: People time
episodes.text: People need things from you — questions, help, decisions. You deal with them one at a time, the way this job always does. Real people, real reactions — this is the human side of the job, as it actually feels.

choice.prompt: Someone you're working with asks you to take on one more thing — extra work, on top of everything already in front of you today.

options.label: Say yes and fit it in
options.outcome: You fit it in. The day runs longer, the work gets done properly — and the person who asked remembers that you said yes.

options.label: Say no, politely
options.outcome: You say no, and you say why. A short, slightly awkward moment — then the rest of your day stays yours.

options.label: Offer a smaller version
options.outcome: You offer the part you can actually do, and by when. Most days that's accepted — saying yes to everything is how this job burns people out.

episodes.title: Hands on
episodes.text: Tools-and-systems time: you work the equipment and the screens of the trade until the thing in front of you does what it should. Skilled, hands-on work — the part where being good at it shows.

trial.title: The check-in
trial.says: Hey — how's that thing coming along that you were working on?
options: It's on track. I'll flag it straight away if I need help or it slips.
Fine.
Honestly? Don't ask. It's a disaster.
trial.explain: The professional reply says where things stand and what happens next — short, honest, no drama.

episodes.title: The routine block
episodes.text: The same block as yesterday: the repeating tasks that never make the brochure. You do them again, carefully, because skipping them is exactly how mistakes happen. The same again tomorrow. This block repeats more than any other part of the job.

episodes.title: It goes wrong
episodes.text: Something goes wrong — it always does, some days. A problem lands on you that was in nobody's plan, and sorting it out is now your job. Unplanned and unavoidable — how the job feels when it pushes back.

episodes.title: The paperwork
episodes.text: End of day: notes, records, the write-up of everything you did. The work isn't finished until it's written down. Nobody's favourite part. It still has to be done, every day.

episodes.title: First Student Logs On
episodes.text: You open your session and greet your student. You sit with just him for the hour. You work with him on math to lift his grades.

episodes.title: Talking Through Homework
episodes.text: You pull up yesterday's worksheet with your next student. You talk through the text together and work the problems step by step. You pause when she gets stuck on question three.

choice.prompt: She stops answering. Do you move on or stay with this problem?

options.label: Stay and work it together
options.outcome: You solve it line by line with her. She finishes the rest on her own.

options.label: Skip it and come back later
options.outcome: You finish the other problems first. You return to it together at the end.

episodes.title: Same Worksheet Again
episodes.text: You open the same practice sheet you used yesterday. You go down the rows and mark what is done. Same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Showing Note Taking
episodes.text: You meet a new student after lunch. You show him how to take short notes while he reads. You have him try it on the next page.

trial.title: Review a worksheet
items: Discuss the text on the page
trial.explain: You start with the page before you solve anything.

episodes.title: Student Freezes Up
episodes.text: You watch your student stall halfway through a test practice set. He goes quiet and will not try the next question. You see his confidence drop in real time.

choice.prompt: He says he cannot do it. What do you do?

options.label: Point out what he got right
options.outcome: You name two steps he did well. He takes a breath and tries again.

options.label: Pause and review progress calmly
options.outcome: You look back at what he finished today. He starts the next one slowly.

options.label: Give him a minute of quiet
options.outcome: You wait while he sits. He picks up his pen when he is ready.

episodes.title: Closing With Encouragement
episodes.text: You finish your last session of the day. You tell your student what she did well today. You leave her with one clear thing to keep practicing.

episodes.title: Morning Numbers Check
episodes.text: You arrive and open yesterday's sales and activity reports. You compare productivity numbers to the goals. You mark one area where costs look high.

trial.title: Find the cost problem
trial.scenario: You review three product lines against their goals. Two meet their targets with steady costs. One meets its sales goal but its activity costs run well over plan.
options: The line with high costs that needs program improvement
A line that met both sales and cost goals
The full sales total for all lines together
trial.explain: You look first at the line where costs run over plan even when sales look fine.

episodes.title: Coordinating Today's Work
episodes.text: You gather the leads for production, sales, and distribution for the day's plan.

chat.text: Production can finish the morning batch by ten.
Sales needs that batch split between two orders today.
Confirm the plan so distribution can schedule the trucks.

episodes.title: Checking Goods Movement
episodes.text: You check goods moving into and out of the facility. The counts match the sheet like yesterday. You sign off and do the same check again tomorrow.

episodes.title: Setting Prices
episodes.text: You sit down with the demand forecast for next week. You look at what customers are likely to order. You set the price and credit terms for one service.

choice.prompt: Demand looks soft for next week. How do you set the price?

options.label: Hold the price steady
options.outcome: You keep the price steady and orders stay slow for the week.

options.label: Lower the price slightly
options.outcome: You lower the price slightly and a few more orders come in.

options.label: Tighten credit terms
options.outcome: You tighten credit terms and late payments drop but new orders stay flat.

episodes.title: Dock Backup
episodes.text: You get word that inbound goods are piling up at the dock. Outbound trucks are waiting and production is slowing. You go to the dock to direct the flow.

choice.prompt: Both inbound and outbound trucks need the dock now. What do you move first?

options.label: Clear outbound goods first
options.outcome: You send the finished goods out and free space for the inbound trucks.

options.label: Bring inbound goods in first
options.outcome: You bring raw goods inside and production keeps running a little longer.

episodes.title: Closing Admin Tasks
episodes.text: You return to your desk to close out the admin work. You confirm schedules and service notes are filed. You leave the desk clear for tomorrow.

episodes.title: First Eye Check
episodes.text: You arrive and bring in your first patient. You sit down with the eye chart and lights low. You check how clearly they see, how the eyes focus and work together.

choice.prompt: The readings are borderline and the morning is already full. Do you run the extra focus and coordination checks now?

options.label: Run the extra checks now
options.outcome: You keep them a few minutes longer and get a clear picture of focus and coordination.

options.label: Note it and move on
options.outcome: You note the borderline result and plan to recheck it at the next visit.

episodes.title: Fitting New Glasses
episodes.text: You bring out the new glasses for a pickup and check the fit on their face.

chat.text: They slide down my nose when I look down.
Can you fix that?

episodes.title: Midmorning Vision Charts
episodes.text: You run the same visual acuity checks again. Same chart, same lights, same notes as yesterday. Same again tomorrow.

episodes.title: Reading Test Results
episodes.text: You sit down with the morning test results. You compare the numbers and look for changes. You write a simple treatment plan for each file.

episodes.title: Pressure Spike Found
episodes.text: You check eye pressure and see a high reading that points toward glaucoma.

choice.prompt: The pressure is high and the patient is worried. What do you do next?

options.label: Recheck and explain referral
options.outcome: You recheck the pressure, explain what you found, and arrange prompt follow-up care.

options.label: Prescribe drops now if allowed
options.outcome: You check state rules, prescribe eye drops where allowed, and set a close recheck.

chat.text: My vision feels fine. Is something wrong?
Do I need medicine today?

episodes.title: Lens Care Talk
episodes.text: You sit with a new contact lens wearer at the end of the day. You go over cleaning, safe wear, and lighting at home. You answer their last questions.

trial.title: Answer about lens care
trial.says: Can I just rinse my contacts with tap water if I run out of solution?
options: No, use only fresh contact solution and clean the case as shown.
Sure, tap water is fine for a night or two.
Just wear them longer and skip cleaning this week.
trial.explain: Fresh solution keeps lenses clean and lowers risk of eye infection.

episodes.title: First Meeting and Measuring
episodes.text: You bring a new patient into the exam room. You ask about pain and daily movement as you start to measure the leg.

choice.prompt: Her ankle is swollen today and size changes during the day. How do you set the measurements?

options.label: Note both morning and swollen size and allow room
options.outcome: You record both measurements and plan extra room in the brace. The fit stays usable when swelling comes up.

options.label: Measure only as it is right now
options.outcome: You record today's size only. The brace feels tight later when the ankle swells.

chat.text: My ankle swells by the afternoon. Mornings are better.
Will the brace still fit later in the day?

episodes.title: Picking Materials and Parts
episodes.text: You sit at the bench with the device design. You pick the plastic, padding, and joint parts to match the shape and support needed.

episodes.title: Testing the New Brace
episodes.text: You fit the brace on the patient and watch her stand and walk. You check the edges, straps, and movement and trim a rough spot for comfort.

trial.title: What needs attention first
trial.scenario: You test the brace while the patient walks. The straps feel even, but one edge digs into the skin. Walking is otherwise steady.
options: Edge digging into the skin
Even pressure from the straps
Steady walking pattern
trial.explain: The digging edge hurts comfort and fit, so you fix that spot first.

episodes.title: Afternoon Care Instructions
episodes.text: You sit with a patient and go over wearing time, cleaning, and skin checks. It is the same talk as yesterday. It will be the same again tomorrow.

episodes.title: Sore Spot Returns
episodes.text: A patient comes back with a red mark where the socket rubs. You test the fit and see the pressure is wrong in one place.

choice.prompt: The socket rubs in one place and the patient waits. What do you do now?

options.label: Adjust the fit now in the clinic
options.outcome: You pad and reshape that spot and test it again. The patient walks out with less pressure on the mark.

options.label: Ask them to wear it one more week
options.outcome: You keep the same fit and check the skin again next week. The red mark is still there at the next visit.

options.label: Take new measurements for a remake
options.outcome: You remeasure and order a new socket shape. The patient uses the old one carefully until it arrives.

episodes.title: Updating Patient Records
episodes.text: You sit at the desk and update charts from today. You log measurements, fit changes, and care instructions given.

episodes.title: Morning Truck Check
episodes.text: You arrive at the truck in the cold yard. You walk around it with your checklist. You look at the mechanical, safety, and emergency equipment.

choice.prompt: One brake light is out. Do you fix it now or after loading?

options.label: Fix it now
options.outcome: You change the bulb and recheck the lights. You start loading a few minutes late.

options.label: Load first, fix after
options.outcome: You load the truck, then come back to the light. You fix it before you move the truck.

episodes.title: Securing The Load
episodes.text: You climb up on the flatbed with your ropes and blocks. You set the blocks tight against the cargo. You throw the chains over and pull the covers down.

trial.title: Secure the cargo
items: Tighten the binders and check the tension
Pull the cover over the load
Throw ropes and chains over the load
trial.explain: You block first, then rope, then tighten, then cover.

episodes.title: Mid Morning Walkaround
episodes.text: You do the same load check you do every day. You walk the sides and look at the ropes and chains. Same as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Checking The Papers
episodes.text: You sit in the cab with the load papers on your lap. You read each line for the weight and contents. You check that nothing is missing or wrong.

episodes.title: Dangerous Goods Placard
episodes.text: You stop before leaving because the load includes dangerous goods. You check the safety papers and placards again. You smell fuel near one valve and step back.

choice.prompt: You see a small leak at the valve. What do you do?

options.label: Stop and follow the safety procedure
options.outcome: You shut the valve, move clear, and call the number on the sheet. You wait for clearance before you touch the load.

options.label: Wipe it and keep going
options.outcome: You wipe the valve and close the doors. The leak continues and you have to stop down the road anyway.

episodes.title: Final Load Look
episodes.text: You walk around the parked truck one last time. You push on the straps and look at the covers. You make sure the cargo is still secure.

episodes.title: Morning Work Order
episodes.text: You arrive at the house and meet the homeowner on the porch. You pull out the work order to go over the rooms together.

choice.prompt: The homeowner waits while you check the order. How do you confirm the work?

options.label: Read the colors and rooms back to them
options.outcome: They nod and point to the right paint cans. You both start clear on what gets painted today.

options.label: Just start working from what you remember
options.outcome: You set up in the wrong corner first. You move everything and lose half an hour.

chat.text: We need the living room walls done today, just the two coats we talked about.
Please keep the paint off the trim and the wood floor.

episodes.title: Covering the Floors
episodes.text: You carry dropcloths into the living room and shake them out over the wood floor. You press masking tape and paper along the baseboards and trim. You check the edges once more before you open any paint.

episodes.title: Filling the Cracks
episodes.text: You walk the walls and spot small cracks and nail holes. You load the caulking gun and press filler into each joint. You scrape it flush with your putty knife and let it set.

trial.title: Fill a crack in order
items: Scrape the filler flush with a putty knife
Find the crack or hole in the wall
Press filler in with a caulking gun
trial.explain: You find the spot first, then fill it, smooth it, and let it set.

episodes.title: Sanding It Smooth
episodes.text: You pick up the sandpaper and work the patched spots in slow circles. You sand, wipe the dust, then sand again. It is the same motion as yesterday, and the same as tomorrow.

episodes.title: Roller Leaves A Drip
episodes.text: You roll paint across the living room wall and see a thick drip running down. You catch it with your brush while it is still wet. The patch area shows through thin behind it.

choice.prompt: The drip is still wet and the patch shows through. What do you do now?

options.label: Smooth the drip now and roll another coat over the patch
options.outcome: The drip flattens out and the second pass covers the patch. The wall dries even.

options.label: Leave it and keep rolling the rest of the wall
options.outcome: The drip dries into a hard ridge. You have to sand it flat later and repaint that section.

options.label: Wipe the drip and touch up just that spot
options.outcome: The wipe leaves a light mark. You still need a full second coat to blend it in.

episodes.title: Second Coat Walls
episodes.text: You pour paint into the tray and load your roller evenly. You apply the finish in steady overlaps from top to bottom. You step back and check the walls for missed spots.

episodes.title: Filing Yesterday's Mail
episodes.text: You sit down and open the filing system. You sort legal correspondence into the right folders, paper and electronic. Same as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Client Call About Details
episodes.text: You meet with a client on video to go over details of their case.

choice.prompt: The client gives you two different dates for the same event. What do you do now?

options.label: Ask which date matches their records
options.outcome: You ask calmly and they check. You note the corrected date to discuss with the team.

options.label: Write down both dates for now
options.outcome: You write both versions in your notes. You flag it to confirm later with records.

chat.text: I sent you the dates, but I'm not sure they're right.
Do you need me to explain what happened again?

episodes.title: Searching Public Records
episodes.text: You search public records and internet sources for facts about the case. You compare what you find to the file notes. You list what supports a cause of action.

episodes.title: Reviewing The Draft Contract
episodes.text: You sit with a draft contract and read it line by line. You edit wording and mark parts to review. You save your version for the file.

trial.title: Find the Missed Detail
trial.scenario: You are reviewing a real estate closing statement before filing. Two pages match the file, but one page has a name spelled differently from the rest.
options: The misspelled name that does not match the file
The page numbers at the bottom
The font used in the headings
trial.explain: The name must match exactly across legal documents before filing.

episodes.title: Missing Trial Exhibit
episodes.text: You are organizing exhibits for trial and one numbered exhibit is not in the folder. The list says it should be there. You check the shelves and the electronic file again.

choice.prompt: The exhibit is still missing and trial prep is due today. What do you do first?

options.label: Tell the attorney what is missing
options.outcome: You tell them which exhibit number is missing. You both decide how to proceed with prep.

options.label: Keep organizing the exhibits you have
options.outcome: You finish sorting the exhibits you do have. You set the gap aside to report clearly.

options.label: Recheck paper and electronic files once more
options.outcome: You do one careful recheck of both places. You confirm whether it is truly missing.

episodes.title: Drafting Tomorrow's Affidavit
episodes.text: You prepare a draft affidavit from the notes and correspondence. You check the wording against the last version. You place it in the filing system for review.

episodes.title: The core work
episodes.text: You start the main work of a Penetration Tester — the core of the job, done properly, start to finish. No audience and no shortcut: this is the thing everything else in the day supports. This is the work the whole job is built around.

episodes.title: People time
episodes.text: A quiet stretch: mostly you and the work. Human contact in this job is the exception, not the rule — long solo runs are the normal texture of the day. Real people, real reactions — this is the human side of the job, as it actually feels.

choice.prompt: A message lands: could you also take on one more thing today — extra work, on top of everything already in front of you?

options.label: Say yes and fit it in
options.outcome: You fit it in. The day runs longer, the work gets done properly — and the person who asked remembers that you said yes.

options.label: Say no, politely
options.outcome: You say no, and you say why. A short, slightly awkward moment — then the rest of your day stays yours.

options.label: Offer a smaller version
options.outcome: You offer the part you can actually do, and by when. Most days that's accepted — saying yes to everything is how this job burns people out.

episodes.title: Hands on
episodes.text: Tools-and-systems time: you work the equipment and the screens of the trade until the thing in front of you does what it should. Skilled, hands-on work — the part where being good at it shows.

trial.title: The check-in
trial.says: Hey — how's that thing coming along that you were working on?
options: It's on track. I'll flag it straight away if I need help or it slips.
Fine.
Honestly? Don't ask. It's a disaster.
trial.explain: The professional reply says where things stand and what happens next — short, honest, no drama.

episodes.title: The routine block
episodes.text: The same block as yesterday: the repeating tasks that never make the brochure. You do them again, carefully, because skipping them is exactly how mistakes happen. The same again tomorrow. This block repeats more than any other part of the job.

episodes.title: It goes wrong
episodes.text: Something goes wrong — it always does, some days. A problem lands on you that was in nobody's plan, and sorting it out is now your job. Unplanned and unavoidable — how the job feels when it pushes back.

episodes.title: The paperwork
episodes.text: End of day: notes, records, the write-up of everything you did. The work isn't finished until it's written down. Nobody's favourite part. It still has to be done, every day.

episodes.title: Cleaning Your Station
episodes.text: You arrive and set your bag down. You wipe down the chair and counter. You run your tools through sterilizing and lay out a clean area.

trial.title: Check the clean
trial.scenario: You finish wiping the station and look it over before your first client. The counter is clear, the chair is wiped, one tool tray is still waiting to be sterilized.
options: Restock your lotions
Sterilize the waiting tray
Turn on the room light
trial.explain: Tools must be sterilized before a client sits down.

episodes.title: First Client Cleanse
episodes.text: You greet your morning client and get her settled in the chair.

chat.text: Should I have washed my face this morning?
You smile and explain you will cleanse her skin now anyway.
Okay, good. My skin feels kind of oily.

episodes.title: Picking the Color
episodes.text: You hold small color swatches near your client's skin in the daylight. You compare two browns to see which fits her skin quality and appearance. She waits while you decide what to suggest.

choice.prompt: The warmer brown looks nice but a little dark for her skin. What do you do?

options.label: Use the darker warm shade
options.outcome: You go ahead with the darker shade. It heals a little stronger than you hoped and she asks about it at her check-in.

options.label: Switch to the softer shade
options.outcome: You switch to the softer shade. It blends in better and she nods when she sees it against her skin.

episodes.title: Same Midday Reset
episodes.text: You wipe the same counter and chair again. You sterilize the same tools and take out the same trash. Same as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Color Looks Too Dark
episodes.text: You cleanse the skin and check the color you just tested. It looks much darker against her freshly cleansed skin than you expected. She goes quiet and looks worried.

choice.prompt: She is waiting and the color looks too strong. What do you do now?

options.label: Pause and wipe it back off
options.outcome: You pause and gently cleanse the test color off. You both look again and talk through a lighter option.

options.label: Keep going as planned
options.outcome: You keep going with the same color. She stays tense in the chair and you spend extra time reassuring her.

options.label: Ask her to pick alone
options.outcome: You ask her to pick the color by herself. She feels unsure and asks you to stay and help her decide.

episodes.title: Notes and Aftercare
episodes.text: You sit down with your client record at the desk. You write down her skin needs and the colors you used today. You show her how to clean the area gently with water and lotion.

episodes.title: The core work
episodes.text: You start the main work of a Personal / Fashion Stylist — the core of the job, done properly, start to finish. No audience and no shortcut: this is the thing everything else in the day supports. This is the work the whole job is built around.

options.outcome: You say no, and you say why. A short, slightly awkward moment — then the rest of your day stays yours.

options.label: Offer a smaller version
options.outcome: You offer the part you can actually do, and by when. Most days that's accepted — saying yes to everything is how this job burns people out.

episodes.title: Hands on
episodes.text: Hands-on time. You make, fix or adjust the real thing in front of you — the part of the job you can touch, and the part where skill is visible. Skilled, hands-on work — the part where being good at it shows.

trial.title: The check-in
trial.says: Hey — how's that thing coming along that you were working on?
options: It's on track. I'll flag it straight away if I need help or it slips.
Fine.
Honestly? Don't ask. It's a disaster.
trial.explain: The professional reply says where things stand and what happens next — short, honest, no drama.

episodes.title: The routine block
episodes.text: The same block as yesterday: the repeating tasks that never make the brochure. You do them again, carefully, because skipping them is exactly how mistakes happen. The same again tomorrow. This block repeats more than any other part of the job.

episodes.title: It goes wrong
episodes.text: Something goes wrong — it always does, some days. A problem lands on you that was in nobody's plan, and sorting it out is now your job. Unplanned and unavoidable — how the job feels when it pushes back.

episodes.title: The paperwork
episodes.text: End of day: notes, records, the write-up of everything you did. The work isn't finished until it's written down. Nobody's favourite part. It still has to be done, every day.

episodes.title: Morning Client Interview
episodes.text: You arrive and set out a clean notepad. You sit down with a new client across the desk. You ask about income, expenses, and insurance coverage. You note tax status, objectives, and risk tolerance.

episodes.title: Working Through Numbers
episodes.text: You sit back at your desk with the morning notes. You add up income against expenses. You look for strategies that fit the client's objectives.

trial.title: Sort the interview steps
items: Match strategies to the client's objectives
Check insurance coverage and tax status
trial.explain: You gather the full picture before you pick a strategy.

episodes.title: Questions About The Plan
episodes.text: You meet the client again to walk through the draft plan. You open the folder so you can answer questions together.

choice.prompt: The client looks unsure about the plan details. How do you answer?

options.label: Explain the purpose in plain words
options.outcome: You walk through each part slowly. The client nods and asks to take the notes home.

options.label: Offer to go over it again tomorrow
options.outcome: You set a time to meet again. The client leaves with the draft folder.

chat.text: What is this part of the plan actually for?
Can you go over the details once more?
I want to be sure I understand before we go on.

episodes.title: Afternoon Portfolio Updates
episodes.text: You sit down to keep client plans up-to-date. You open each portfolio and check the same boxes as yesterday. You save the files and move to the next one. Tomorrow will look the same.

episodes.title: Plan Needs Rethinking
episodes.text: You sit down for a regular review of a client's account. You see a job change and lower income than last quarter. You know the current plan no longer fits and needs reassessment.

choice.prompt: The plan no longer matches the client's life change. What do you do first?

options.label: Pause and flag it for reassessment
options.outcome: You mark the account for a full review. You call the client to schedule a talk about next steps.

options.label: Leave the plan as it is for now
options.outcome: You keep the portfolio unchanged today. The mismatch stays on your list for the next review.

options.label: Adjust the plan on your own
options.outcome: You draft a small update to match the new income. You wait for the client to approve it.

episodes.title: Keeping Files Current
episodes.text: You sit at your desk to manage the day's portfolios. You enter today's notes and keep each client plan up-to-date. You close the files when everything matches.

episodes.title: Checking the Porch Wall
episodes.text: You arrive at a small house and walk the outside wall. You crouch down and look for where pests get in. You check the damp spot for porosity and damage.

trial.title: Find the Source First
trial.scenario: You see old droppings in the corner, a damp soft spot in the wall, and a clean closed vent. You need to find the source and extent of damage first.
options: The damp soft spot in the wall
The clean closed vent
The swept front step
trial.explain: The soft damp spot shows access and possible damage to check first.

episodes.title: Explaining the Options
episodes.text: You sit at the kitchen table with the client and lay out what you found.

choice.prompt: The client asks what to do next. What do you recommend?

options.label: Recommend sealing the gap and a follow-up spray
options.outcome: You explain the treatment and how sealing helps prevent return. The client nods and agrees to the plan.

options.label: Recommend only a one-time spray
options.outcome: You explain what the single spray will and will not do. The client books just the spray for today.

chat.text: Can you just spray today and be done with it?
Do we need to do anything after you leave?

episodes.title: Locking Up for Fumigation
episodes.text: You tape warning signs on each door of the small building. You test each door and lock them to secure the area. You stand by the front door to keep it clear.

choice.prompt: A worker says he left tools inside and wants to run in quickly. What do you do?

options.label: Keep the doors locked and keep him out
options.outcome: You tell him the area stays shut until fumigation is done. He waits outside and gets his tools later.

options.label: Let him in fast to grab them
options.outcome: You unlock the door and he goes inside the warning area. You lock it again behind him and note the delay.

episodes.title: Same Spray Route
episodes.text: You walk the row of ditches and catch basins with your sprayer. You spray each one the same way as yesterday. Tomorrow you will do it again.

episodes.title: Dusting the Cabinets
episodes.text: You kneel in the kitchen and dust powder along the back of the wood cabinets. You work slow so it lands thin and even. You wipe your hands and check the line.

episodes.title: Writing the Day Down
episodes.text: You sit in the van and open your work log. You write what you inspected, sprayed, and locked up today. You close the book and head back.

episodes.title: Morning Food Bowls
episodes.text: You unlock the kennel row and check the feeding chart on the wall. You fill each bowl to the marked line and top up the water dishes. You set the bowls down one by one as the dogs crowd forward.

episodes.title: Laundry and Kennels
episodes.text: You load yesterday's blankets into the washer and start the same cycle. You scrub the pens and mop the floor with disinfectant. You fold the dry load and stack it back on the shelf.

episodes.title: Morning Health Walk
episodes.text: You walk the rows slowly and look at each animal. You check eyes, coats, and how they move and eat. You pause at a terrier sitting apart from its water bowl.

trial.title: Spot the sick one
trial.scenario: You see three pens. One dog eats its full bowl and drinks water. One cat naps curled up after eating. One dog breathes fast and leaves its food alone.
options: The dog breathing fast and skipping food
The dog eating its full bowl
The cat napping after eating
trial.explain: Skipping food and breathing fast are signs to check for illness or injury.

episodes.title: Mixing Lunch Formulas
episodes.text: You sit down at the prep counter with the instruction cards. You measure kibble, powder supplement, and water for each animal. You stir each mix and set the labeled bowls out to serve.

episodes.title: Limping Dog Help
episodes.text: You find the boarder beagle limping in its pen and kneel to look closer.

choice.prompt: His leg looks swollen and he yelps when you touch it. What do you do?

options.label: Clean and bandage it yourself
options.outcome: You rinse the leg, wrap it lightly, and keep him quiet in his pen to watch him.

options.label: Call the vet now
options.outcome: You call the vet, describe the swelling and yelping, and follow what they tell you to do.

chat.text: He was fine this morning, now he will not put weight on that back leg.
Do you want me to hold him while you look, or should I call the vet now?

episodes.title: Evening Water Check
episodes.text: You start the last feeding round and check every water bowl. You see the new cat has eaten little of its special diet. You stand with the scoop and reread its feeding instructions.

choice.prompt: The card says one small scoop at this hour. The cat looks hungry but left food earlier. What do you do?

options.label: Stick to the card amount
options.outcome: You give the one scoop listed and note how much is left for the next check.

options.label: Add extra food
options.outcome: You add a little extra and write down what you gave and what was left before.

episodes.title: Morning Feeding Round
episodes.text: You arrive and unlock the holding pens. You check the feeding board on the wall. You fill water bowls and scoop morning feed for each animal.

episodes.title: Checking Every Animal
episodes.text: You walk the row slowly and look at each animal. You watch how they stand, eat, and breathe. You notice one cat sitting apart and not touching food.

choice.prompt: The cat is quiet and leaves its food alone. What do you do next?

options.label: Look closer for signs of illness
options.outcome: You kneel down and check its eyes, nose, and posture. You see it is dull and you keep watching it through the morning.

options.label: Leave it and move on
options.outcome: You finish the rest of the row. The full bowl is still there when you come back later.

episodes.title: Washing Bowls and Bedding
episodes.text: You gather the laundry and empty food bowls. You wash, rinse, and stack the same bowls as yesterday. You wipe the pens and put clean bedding back down.

episodes.title: Mixing Midday Formulas
episodes.text: You sit at the prep counter with the instruction cards. You measure food and liquid formula for each pen. You add the listed supplements and stir each mix.

trial.title: Mix the feed correctly
items: Stir in the prescribed medication supplement
Set out the labeled bowl for the animal
Read the feeding card for amounts
Pour the measured formula and food together
trial.explain: You always read the instructions before you measure and mix anything.

episodes.title: Limping Dog in Pen
episodes.text: You see a dog holding up one paw after the midday feed.

choice.prompt: The dog has a cut pad and will not put weight on it. What do you do?

options.label: Clean it and give basic first treatment
options.outcome: You clean the cut and keep the dog still in a clean pen. You watch for swelling or bleeding.

options.label: Call the veterinarian now
options.outcome: You call the vet and describe the cut and the limp. You keep the dog quiet until you get advice.

options.label: Put him back with the others
options.outcome: You lead him back to the group pen. He sits down and keeps the sore paw lifted.

chat.text: Did you see him limping on the back leg?
There is a small cut on the pad.

episodes.title: Evening Water and Reset
episodes.text: You walk through again with fresh water and feed. You check bowls and top up what is low. You straighten the pens and disinfect the tools for tomorrow.

episodes.title: Morning Prescriptions
episodes.text: You arrive and open the queue of new prescriptions. You read each one for accuracy and check what ingredients are needed. You set aside one where the dose does not look suitable.

episodes.title: Checking The Stock
episodes.text: You stand at the counter and check a delivery of tablets. You look at the labels for identity and strength. You hold one bottle to the light to check its purity.

trial.title: What needs attention first
trial.scenario: You are assessing a batch of medications for identity, strength, and purity. Two bottles match their labels clearly. One bottle has a strength on the label that does not match the order.
options: The bottle with the wrong strength
A bottle that matches its label
The clean shelf behind you
trial.explain: You check the wrong strength first because it affects patient safety.

episodes.title: Advice At Counter
episodes.text: You sit down with an older man picking up two new pills.

choice.prompt: He asks about side effects and storage while you see a possible interaction. What do you cover first?

options.label: Explain the interaction and what to do
options.outcome: You tell him not to take them together and call his prescriber with him. He waits while you phone.

options.label: Explain dosage and storage only
options.outcome: You show him the dose times and where to store the bottles. You flag the interaction to follow up after he leaves.

chat.text: Can I take these together? And where do I keep them?
The small one made me feel dizzy last time.

episodes.title: Files And Counts
episodes.text: You sit back at the computer and update pharmacy files and patient profiles. You enter charges and count inventory. Same as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Too Many Refills
episodes.text: You scan prescribing trends and see one patient refilling early every month. The pattern points to excessive usage and a harmful interaction. You have to act before the next fill.

choice.prompt: The refill request is in front of you. What do you do?

options.label: Hold the refill and call the prescriber
options.outcome: You put the refill on hold and phone the prescriber. You note the compliance concern in the profile.

options.label: Dispense and add a warning note
options.outcome: You fill it once and attach a clear warning note. You log the pattern for the prescriber to review.

options.label: Ask the patient to come in
options.outcome: You call the patient back to review their use. You listen and explain the risk of taking too much.

episodes.title: Controlled Drugs Log
episodes.text: You close the day by updating the registry for narcotics and controlled drugs. You match each entry to the prescription file. You lock the cabinet and sign the control record.
